1.text:
The birds were chirping merrily outside Harry's window as soon as he woke up. Rubbing his eyes groggily, Harry stretched his body and fumbled for the alarm clock on his table.

"Oh dear! It's eight o'clock! I'm so late for school!" Harry cried anxiously as he bolted out of his bed and rushed to the bathroom.

After brushing his teeth, Harry ran out of his bedroom. His mother had prepared a scrumptious breakfast. The aroma of bacon and eggs wafted in the air. However, Harry went straight to the living room and put on his school shoes.

"Where are you going, Harry? Your breakfast is on the table!" Mother shouted from the kitchen.

"Sorry, Mum, I'm late for school!" Harry yelled a hasty goodbye before running out of the house.

Mother could barely react in time. She came out of the kitchen, clearly bewildered. Why would Harry be making his way to school? Mother wondered. Harry, dressed in his school uniform, was making a beeline for the bus stop. However, it was a Saturday morning! Mother shook her head and fished out her mobile phone, ready to give her absent-minded son a call.
1.title: Harry Oversleeps

10.text:
It was the annual beach cleaning day. Mr Tan brought Class 6A to the beach for a meaningful task — to clean up the place. The students were equipped with gloves, trash bags and thongs. Rubbish like plastic bags, metal cans and used tissue paper was scattered all over the shore. It was certainly an unsightly scene.

"Remember, it is important that we stay safe throughout the activity. Do not go near the sea and stay within the parameters," Mr Tan instructed as he handed out the equipment. Soon after, every student got down to work.

Barely ten minutes had passed since the start of the activity when James, the class clown, turned to his friends and cried, "The weather is killing me! Shall we just head to the nearby eatery and grab some drinks?"

Some of the boys nodded, eager to stop what they were doing. However, a boy named Paul refused.

"I think we should be responsible and complete our task. Even if we want to take a break, we should seek Mr Tan's permission," Paul said firmly. The other boys rolled their eyes but continued picking up the trash.
10.title: Beach Cleaning Day

2.text:
Marilyn had been looking forward to Racial Harmony Day. She was excited about wearing an ethnic costume to school and exploring different stalls that would showcase the cultures in Singapore. Besides, her class had been selected to perform a skit during assembly. The skit was a funny story about three friends trying out different cuisines.

"Have you practised your lines?" Marilyn's sister, Jane, asked.

"Yes, I've done so multiple times! However, I'm still feeling quite jittery about it," Marilyn replied as she admired the Indian costume hung in her closet.

"Don't worry about it!" Jane reassured her kindly. "You will do fine. Just don't forget your lines!"

Marilyn gave a weak smile and nodded. They had been rehearsing for the performance for the past few weeks. Jane was right. The last thing Marilyn wanted was to forget her lines out of anxiety.

Before she knew it, Racial Harmony Day had arrived. Marilyn put on her beautiful Indian costume, tied her hair in a braid and made her way to school. It was finally the day for her to showcase what she got.
2.title: Racial Harmony Day

3.text:
It was Jason's first day at his school's photography club. While he had minimal photo-taking experience, he was intrigued by the photos displayed by the club during the co-curricular activities fair.

"Is this your first time using a digital camera?" Tom, the club president, asked Jason. He had a huge, black digital camera hung around his neck.

Jason nodded and replied, "That's right. I've never tried taking photos of scenery before. This camera looks heavy."

Tom let out a soft chuckle and shook his head. He took the lanyard of the camera off of his neck and passed the gadget to Jason. "Here, hold it. It is not heavy at all! In fact, you can hang it around your neck, just like I did!"

Jason immediately did as Tom suggested and he felt like a professional photographer! Indeed, the camera was not too heavy. That day, Tom taught him the various functions of the camera and how to manoeuvre the buttons. Jason even tried taking a few close-up shots of a blooming sunflower. He was proud of himself for taking such artistic looking photographs!
3.title: Photography Club

4.text:
Peter and Sarah walked into a gift shop. Their mother's birthday was around the corner, and the children intended to buy her a gift. The moment they stepped into the shop, they were overwhelmed by the wide array of unique gifts. All around them were artificial flowers, decorative items and greeting cards.

"Look at this mug! It says here 'Best Mum Ever'!" Peter gushed as he lifted a purple ceramic mug.

"This looks like something Mum might like!" Sarah added, holding up a photo frame decorated with flower petals.

The two of them spent close to an hour looking at all the wonderful gifts that were sold in the shop. Unfortunately, most of the items were quite expensive. Even the flowers would cost them fifteen dollars per bouquet.

"How much money have we got in total?" Sarah asked. Peter counted the money he had in his wallet. Together, they had managed to save up twelve dollars. Both of them sighed in disappointment.

"Ah! I have an idea!" Peter exclaimed. "Why don't we get some coloured paper and make our own flowers?"
4.title: Mother's Birthday

5.text:
Leah was never the most athletic child in her family. However, just a few days back, her father had promised her that he would quit smoking if she took up swimming.

Burning with a keen sense of anticipation, Leah attended her first one-to-one swimming lesson. As soon as she arrived at the swimming complex, she saw her coach waiting for her with a kind smile on his face.

"Good morning, Leah!" Coach greeted her warmly. "Are you ready for your first lesson?"

"Yes! Let's begin!" Leah answered enthusiastically.

Then, the swimming lesson commenced. Leah felt rather apprehensive upon being submerged in the water for the first time. Nevertheless, she got through the training with determination.

"Well done for your first lesson, Leah! If we keep up with this pace, you will be able to master the breaststroke in no time," Coach praised Leah at the end of their first swimming lesson. Leah thanked her coach and bade him goodbye before heading to the locker room. There, she saw her father sitting on a bench, showing her his subtle yet unwavering support.
5.title: Leah's Determination

6.text:
The moment Ken stepped into the mall, his attention was drawn to a commotion in a fast food restaurant. A middle-aged lady, dressed in a neat office attire, was screaming hysterically at a young boy. Splattered around them were puddles of purple fizzy liquid and French fries. The lady's pristine white top also sported a huge purple stain.

"Look at what you've done, you mischievous boy!" the lady roared in anger as she gestured to her attire with trembling hands.

The little boy looked petrified. Lowering his head, he dared not make any eye contact with the incensed lady as he mumbled an apology. However, the lady could not be appeased. Ken could tell that she was most likely a businesswoman working in the vicinity.

Some passers-by whipped out their phones to take photos or videos of the commotion, while others were trying to placate the furious lady.

"I'm sorry, Miss. Please forgive this young boy. I have some wet tissues for you," the manager of the restaurant tried his best to calm the lady down. Still scowling, the middle-aged lady grabbed the wet tissues and stormed off.
6.title: A Commotion

7.text:
The sun beat down with fiery intensity. My parents brought my brother, John, and me to a hawker centre. The place was overflowing with diners and it was almost impossible to spot an empty table. Vendors were busily preparing piping hot dishes while long queues formed in front of every stall.

"Why do we have to eat here? It's so stuffy and crowded!" John whined.

I could not disagree with his sentiment. Fishing out my handkerchief, I wiped my forehead that was dotted with perspiration.

"This place sells the best duck rice," Father replied. "Besides, we can take this opportunity to experience the hawker culture in Singapore. Hawker centres are a part of our way of life."

Both John and I were skeptical at first. However, we went along with our parents' plan. Many diners showed consideration by returning their trays after they finished their meals. Soon, we were able to find an empty table. Father ordered a delectable duck feast for us.

"Wow! This tastes amazing!" I gushed, having tasted the crispy duck skin. Even John was savouring the food contentedly. With a grin on my face, I stuffed my handkerchief into my pocket and dug in.
7.title: Hawker Centres

8.text:
Lynn had a bad experience working on a Science project with two other group mates, Oliver and Mary. Oliver was in the swimming team and often had to represent their school in competitions. As such, he was busy most of the time. On the other hand, Mary was simply uninterested in helping out with the project. Even when she turned up for project meetings, she would be preoccupied with her phone.

"Mary, could you please work on your part of the project? The deadline for our project proposal is this Friday," Lynn reminded her in displeasure.

"Oh, don't worry too much about it. I can easily get the needed information by surfing the net. An hour is enough!" Mary gave a nonchalant reply while being deeply engrossed in her phone.

Lynn could only sigh in exasperation. Meanwhile, Oliver was already packing up, all ready to leave their project meeting half an hour early.

"Sorry! I promise to complete my part of the project by tonight. I have to rush for my training now. See you again!" Oliver said as he hastily prepared to leave. However, he would never fulfil what he had promised. Lynn could only blame her ill luck for being grouped with irresponsible members like them.
8.title: Group Projects

9.text:
Eating raw fish did not sound like a good idea. "It's a delicacy in Japan," people had been telling me. That did not seem to make it any more appetising. Raw fish is raw fish, delicacy or not.

All that, however, changed during my last trip to Japan before the pandemic struck. I remember strolling into a fish market, together with my parents, on a cold evening. The air smelled briny and fresh at the same time. My parents brought me to a restaurant where nothing but raw fish was served.

"Give it a try, Jenny. I'm sure you will like it," Mother said with a wink.

"Come on, Mum," I murmured, blatantly showing them my dissatisfaction. "It's just going to taste like the sea! It's nauseating!"

"It doesn't taste anything like the sea, I promise," Father reassured me as he picked up a piece of salmon using his chopsticks. Since he offered to feed me the 'delicacy', I relented. Begrudgingly, I opened my mouth and ate the bright orange fish, expecting to be attacked by a rancid taste. To my surprise, the cold and fresh fish tasted delicious! I found myself reaching for the second piece.
9.title: Trying Something New
